title: An accepted candidate carrying `tRNS`
why: `accepted-candidate.png` is an ordinary colour raster and carries no encoding rule, so a palette file with a `tRNS` chunk is legal. A decoder that hardcodes alpha to `255` reads its pixels as opaque red and the candidate gate passes; a browser applies the transparency and the gate fires. Same hash-valid bytes, two verdicts — so the decoder must apply `tRNS` for palette, greyscale and RGB alike. The expected verdict here is the one a correct decoder reaches: alpha `0` against the candidate's `255` is a per-channel distance of 255.
